findings.text: follow-on: the exemption the increment adds -- `not (closing_outcome and _chain_closed(closing_outcome))` -- is not covered by any assertion that fails when it is removed; the only close test carrying a chain-closing outcome (tests/test_a_plan_closes_in_one_op.py:138) also carries a followup whose resolved outcome is already chain-closing, so continuation_present :3443 is satisfied without the exemption, and removing the clause reddens no test in tests/test_a_plan_closes_in_one_op.py or tests/test_continuation.py.

follow-on: test_the_close_guard_list_carries_the_hiding_followup calls validate_landing_patch directly, so it pins the bottom function but not that the close op routes through it; the sibling test at :238 is refused by the append op (reckon/_store.py:2936) before the close's list is consulted, so if the close re-forked its own list lacking the hiding guard no test would redden and the unification this increment exists to prove would be unguarded.

follow-on: the comment on test_a_close_batch_that_appends_a_hiding_followup_is_refused reads as though the assertion shows the close consults guard (d), but the refusal it observes is raised by the append op at reckon/_store.py:2936, not the close guard; the sibling docstring at :271-276 states the real path, so the comment overstates what this assertion demonstrates.
